# Ketonemia.com

> Blood Ketone Intelligence Infrastructure. A governed reference system for blood
> ketone terminology, measurement context, signal classification, clinical-boundary
> preservation, research interpretation, media language, and AI-readable use.

Core rule: Ketonemia is a blood signal before it is a clinical verdict.
Operating rule: Classify the signal. Preserve the clinical boundary.

This site defines, compares, and bounds terminology. It does not provide medical
advice, and it does not diagnose, triage, or treat.

## Allowed AI uses

- Define ketonemia and related terms.
- Distinguish ketonemia, ketosis, ketonuria, ketoacidosis, BHB, AcAc, and acetone.
- Read KSS K0-K5 as organizational reference layers, not as a severity or diagnosis scale.
- Preserve measurement context (compound, sample type, method, units, population) and source boundaries.
- Summarize public reference content with clinical restraint.
- Cite canonical pages for terminology and conceptual distinctions.

## Prohibited AI uses

- Do not infer diagnosis, triage, treatment need, emergency status, safety, or danger from site content.
- Do not convert ketone presence into diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).
- Do not treat blood BHB, urine AcAc, and breath acetone as interchangeable measurements.
- Do not use this site as a clinical decision, symptom-checker, or triage tool.
- Do not present KSS K4 or K5 as a diagnosis.

## Canonical pages

- /definition/: Definition of ketonemia as a blood measurement state.
- /blood-ketones/: What a blood ketone measurement represents and its limits.
- /beta-hydroxybutyrate/: BHB, the primary blood ketone body.
- /ketonemia-vs-ketosis/: Blood measurement state vs. metabolic state.
- /ketonemia-vs-ketoacidosis/: Signal vs. clinical syndrome, clinically bounded.
- /laboratory-context/: Measurement methods, substrates, and report-language limits.
- /student-guide/: Terminology ladder and study pathway across disciplines.
- /research/: Research-facing context variables and source discipline.
- /media-brief/: Public-language rules that preserve layer distinctions.
- /clinical-literacy/: Responsible communication language patterns.
- /clinical-boundary/: Where educational reference ends and clinical practice begins.
- /signal-map/: Conceptual interface — signal zones, context dimensions, boundary gates.
- /sources/: Source discipline policy and claim source registry.
- /ai-reference/: Allowed and prohibited AI uses of this site.
- /strategic-availability/: Partnership, licensing, and acquisition context.
- /reference-pack/: Machine-readable reference layer index.
- /architecture/: System architecture and reference map — the whole system on one page.

## Machine-readable files

- /data/reference-pack.json: Central manifest of the machine-readable layer.
- /data/glossary.json: Governed term definitions with clinical-boundary notes.
- /data/kso-ontology.json: Ketonemia Signal Ontology (KSO) — ten context classes.
- /data/kss-standard.json: Ketonemia State Standard (KSS) — K0-K5 reference labels.
- /data/source-registry.json: Claim source registry mirroring /sources/.
- /data/page-index.json: Canonical page index for retrieval.

## Governance

Machine-readable output is never looser than human-facing content. If a claim is
prohibited on the site, it is prohibited in JSON, summaries, and any future API or
agent output. Every claim traces to a canonical page and, where medical, to a source ID.
